The maximum eccentricity is the longest shortest path between any two nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [unconnected]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, computes maximum diameter across all connected components. If `False`, returns `None` for disconnected graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Maximum eccentricity (diameter), or `None` if disconnected (when `unconnected=False`). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Find the diameter of a path graph: ::: {#919876f5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5) diameter = graph.get_max_eccentricity() # Returns 4 (end-to-end distance) diameter ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 4 ``` ::: :::
